answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. This design turns the attacker's greatest weapon — scale — into its weakest point, because scale is exactly what becomes unaffordable to maintain. Consider a juniper as the anchor of the cost.
